title: The service that keeps restarting

source.title: bitcoind.service: Start request repeated too quickly (bitcoin/bitcoin issue #26718)

brief:
**ALERT 02:05 · batch-02 · export-worker down, nightly exports missing**

Yesterday the export-worker package was upgraded to 2.0 (`/etc/export-worker/CHANGES`). Since then the service flaps: systemd starts it, it dies at once, systemd tries again, and after a few seconds it stops trying.

The night shift ran `systemctl restart export-worker` three times. "It just fails again, or refuses with *Start request repeated too quickly*."

Don't restart it again. Read what systemd says about each attempt, fix the unit properly, and leave the worker running as the `exporter` user, started at boot. Don't hide the problem with `Restart=always` or a bigger start limit.

tasks.title: Read why it dies, then fix the unit
tasks.text:
`systemctl status export-worker` shows only the last lines. `journalctl -u export-worker` shows every attempt and why it failed. `systemd-analyze verify` checks a unit file without starting it.

There are two faults left over from the upgrade. One stops systemd before the program even runs; the other shows up once the first is fixed. Fix both in a way the next restart and the next boot will use. Done when `verify` is clean, every environment file the unit needs exists and sets `EXPORT_DIR`, and systemd has loaded the new unit.
hints: The journal says `Failed to load environment files: No such file or directory`. `systemd-analyze verify /etc/systemd/system/export-worker.service` says `Command /usr/local/bin/export-worker is not executable`. `cat /etc/export-worker/CHANGES`.

`sudo cp /etc/export-worker/worker.env.example /etc/export-worker/worker.env`, then in `sudo systemctl edit --full export-worker` set `ExecStart=/opt/export-worker/bin/export-worker --queue nightly`. After editing the file directly, run `sudo systemctl daemon-reload`.

questions.prompt: Which command checks a unit file and reports the missing program without starting the service?
questions.format: command with subcommand, without the unit

questions.prompt: By default, how many starts within 10 seconds does systemd allow before it refuses with "Start request repeated too quickly"?

checks.describe: systemd-analyze verify is clean; the environment file exists and sets EXPORT_DIR; User=exporter kept; no daemon-reload pending

tasks.title: Get it out of the start limit
tasks.text:
The unit file is fixed, but the service is still in the failed state, and inside the 10-second window systemd refuses new starts. Clear the failed state and the start counter, start the worker, and watch it for a while: a worker that dies again a second later is not fixed.

Done when export-worker runs as `exporter`, keeps the same PID, writes `/var/lib/export-worker/heartbeat`, and starts at boot.
hints: `systemctl show -p NRestarts,Result,StartLimitBurst export-worker` shows the counters. There is one `systemctl` subcommand that resets a failed unit.
`sudo systemctl reset-failed export-worker && sudo systemctl start export-worker`, then `systemctl status export-worker` twice, a few seconds apart: same Main PID, `active (running)`.

questions.prompt: Which systemctl subcommand clears a unit's failed state and its start counter?

checks.describe: export-worker runs as exporter with a stable PID, writes its heartbeat and starts at boot

walkthrough:
### What was broken
The 2.0 package moved the program to `/opt/export-worker/bin/` and the settings to an environment file, but the unit still had the 1.x paths:
1. `EnvironmentFile=/etc/export-worker/worker.env` did not exist. systemd reads it **before** it starts the program, so each try ended with `Failed to load environment files: No such file or directory` and `result 'resources'`.
2. `ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/export-worker` pointed at a file that no longer exists. Once the env file is there, the journal shows `status=203/EXEC`.
3. `Restart=on-failure` with `RestartSec=300ms` used up the start limit (`StartLimitBurst=5` in `StartLimitIntervalSec=10s`) within seconds: `Start request repeated too quickly`. After that, a manual `restart` inside the window is refused at once.

### Task 1
```bash
systemctl status export-worker
journalctl -u export-worker -n 20            # Failed to load environment files ... Start request repeated too quickly
sudo systemd-analyze verify /etc/systemd/system/export-worker.service   # Command /usr/local/bin/export-worker is not executable
cat /etc/export-worker/CHANGES
sudo cp /etc/export-worker/worker.env.example /etc/export-worker/worker.env
sudo sed -i 's|/usr/local/bin/export-worker|/opt/export-worker/bin/export-worker|' /etc/systemd/system/export-worker.service
sudo systemd-analyze verify /etc/systemd/system/export-worker.service   # no output
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
```
*Why the reload:* systemd keeps its own parsed copy of every unit. Until you reload, `start` still uses the old one, and `systemctl status` warns `changed on disk`. `systemctl edit --full` reloads for you. A `-` before the path (`EnvironmentFile=-/etc/...`) makes the file optional. That is right for optional settings, but here the worker needs `EXPORT_DIR`, so the file belongs on disk.

### Task 2
```bash
systemctl show -p NRestarts,Result export-worker
sudo systemctl reset-failed export-worker
sudo systemctl start export-worker
sleep 5; systemctl status export-worker      # active (running), same Main PID
sudo cat /var/lib/export-worker/heartbeat   # the directory is exporter's (0750)
```
*Why not raise the limit:* the start limit is what stopped a broken service from restarting forever and flooding the journal. Read the first failure in the journal, not the last line: the last line only says that systemd gave up.

**Source (adapted):** [bitcoind.service: Start request repeated too quickly (bitcoin/bitcoin #26718)](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/26718): the service failed, restarted five times and hit the start limit. The reporter found in `journalctl -e` that the `ExecStart=` path was wrong, corrected it, and the service started. The missing environment file is added from the same kind of package upgrade.
